I recently graduated from college debt free.

How do you do it?

I guess that could be managed in Canada, but it must be really expensive in the US, with the manuals, the fees, the transportation...

I went to a community college and then transferred to a state school. Tuition is expensive but not that expensive in California. Tuition is around $7,000 per year which is affordable if you work full time and live with parents. It requires sacrifices, sure, but in the end you'll be able to do stuff that other people won't be able to do like buy a house.
Community college is the key that so many people look over. It is SO much cheaper than a university and just the same, if not better, education.

Yup, pretty much this. The irony is that some of the teachers I took at the CC taught classes at the state college as well. Even further irony is that when I got the state college some of those teachers also taught at private universities like University of Southern California (Tuition for 1 year: 48k). Exact same class. The only difference is we were paying around $60 for the class while the people at the state university were paying north of $700 (and for the USC example: $4,800...). Another difference is that at the CC level a lot of the teachers were actually working in the industry so you get that extra insight as well. The teachers at the state college were pretty much book smart but in terms of how it was actually implemented in the real world, they had no clue.

I went to a CC, ended up doing 4 years there because of a last minute major change. Total college costs were around 1500 for four years. My first paycheck from the job I got directly because of my CC doubled my investment.

Shave. Seriously guys, get rid of those expensive multi-blade monstrosities and cans of goo. Buy yourself a real razor like a Merkur and load it double-edge razor blades such as Astra. Get a tube of Proraso shave soap, a brush and a bowl, and you're set. Much more economical in the long run since the blades only cost about $12CAD for 100. You also get a much more comfortable shave. You'll never look back.
I love my Merkur razor and Astra blades, but I just use Barbasol for cream. Would switching to a shave soap like Proraso make much of a difference?

To me it does make a big difference. I find Barbasol to be a rather low quality soap. Proraso whipped by hand has the right amount of slickness and cushion. It's a great starter soap and you can get it in either a tub (which is the denser form) or as I prefer in a tube (which is the creamier form of the same stuff). Once you figure out how to whip up a great lather you'll probably want to branch out and experiment with different soaps.

For me, shaving is sort of a hobby. I like trying different razors, blades, soaps, brushes, and techniques. I enjoy the process and do it with care. There's a zen to it. On weekends when I have plenty of time I like to use a straight razor. There's not too many things which focus your mind like those!

I haven't had an on-demand antivirus installed for years and I have never gotten a virus. All it takes is attentiveness/savvy to avoid that garbage from getting into your system

Don't just click next all the way through an installer. Pay attention. Check the "custom" or "advanced" install options every time as well. Failing to do so is how you end up with tons of adware/malware/PUPs on your system.

If I had a nickel for every time I had to remove Optimizer Pro from somebody's computer, I could by groceries for a month with the earnings.

Also, treat Word docs and PDF's with the same amount of caution you would give to unknown .exe's. They are basically executables for all intents and purposes.

Edit: Also, for the love of all that is holy, use an up-to-date and modern browser. If I see another computer where the only browser is IE9 because the person thought that updating Windows was too much effort, I will bitch-slap that person. The security vulnerabilities are real.

And do yourselves a favor and grab CryptoPrevent. It stops Cryptowall and other ransomware from being able to hook into your system by changing the permissions of the directories they are known to launch from. It isn't a program that constantly runs so there is no footprint, and it's worth doing to help prevent having all of your personal info RSA-2048 encrypted.

I am exactly the same as you. I haven't had a any antivirus installed on my current machine and I built it ages ago. It's honestly not that difficult, like you said, simply just paying attention to what you are clicking is all that you need to do.
